_meta.indication: ZURZUVAE is indicated for the treatment of postpartum depression (PPD) in adults.

pivotal_trials.population: Female subjects with severe PPD, aged 18 to 45 years, meeting DSM-5 criteria for a major depressive episode with onset in the third trimester or within 4 weeks of delivery, with HAMD-17 scores >=26 at baseline
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in the HAMD-17 total score at Day 15
pivotal_trials.n: N=195 (50 mg ZURZUVAE N=98; placebo N=97)
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean change from baseline in HAMD-17 at Day 15: -15.6 (ZURZUVAE) vs -11.6 (placebo); placebo-subtracted difference -4.0 (95% CI -6.3, -1.7); p=0.0007

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, multicenter study using another zuranolone capsule formulation approximately equivalent to 40 mg of ZURZUVAE
pivotal_trials.population: Female subjects with severe PPD, aged 18 to 45 years, meeting DSM-IV criteria for a major depressive episode with onset in the third trimester or within 4 weeks of delivery
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in the HAMD-17 total score at Day 15
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean change from baseline in HAMD-17 at Day 15: -17.8 (zuranolone) vs -13.6 (placebo); placebo-subtracted difference -4.2 (95% CI -6.9, -1.5); p=0.0028

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=5% and greater than placebo) were somnolence, dizziness, diarrhea, fatigue, nasopharyngitis, and urinary tract infection. In Study 1 somnolence occurred in 36% of 50 mg ZURZUVAE patients vs 6% placebo; dizziness 13% vs 9%. Primary safety concern is CNS depressant effects.
target_moa: Zuranolone is a neuroactive steroid GABAA receptor positive allosteric modulator; its mechanism of action in PPD is thought to be related to its positive allosteric modulation of GABAA receptors.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: IMPAIRED ABILITY TO DRIVE OR ENGAGE IN OTHER POTENTIALLY HAZARDOUS ACTIVITIES — ZURZUVAE causes driving impairment due to CNS depressant effects; patients should not drive until at least 12 hours after administration during the 14-day treatment course.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held because the drug is not the first in its class and the application did not raise scientific or technical matters that would benefit from advisory committee discussion.

basis.text: The PPD data suggested the potential for substantial benefit over existing therapy, so the application was granted a Priority review and, as a new molecular entity, reviewed on an 8-month clock.

citations.quote: PPD data continued to suggest the potential for substantial benefit over existing therapy on preliminary review. Thus, the application was granted a Priority review and, as a new molecular entity (NME), was reviewed on an 8-month clock.

summary.text: Zuranolone (ZURZUVAE) was granted Fast Track designation for PPD (February 2, 2022) and Breakthrough Therapy Designation, and NDA 217369 received Priority review as a new molecular entity, reviewed on an 8-month clock. It was approved for PPD in adults via standard (non-accelerated) approval.
